h: Top Tips for a Smooth Chessington Day
p: A bit of planning makes a huge difference at a big theme park. Download the park app or grab a map when you arrive, and work out your must-do rides first. Many families head straight for the busiest rides at opening time, while others start at the back of the park and work their way forward, beating the crowds. Check the height restrictions in advance too, so you don't end up with a disappointed little one at the front of the queue.

The animals are a brilliant way to break up the day. Zufari: Ride into Africa takes you through a safari-style landscape with giraffes, rhinos, zebras and more, and the Wanyama Village and Reserve gives you the chance to get closer to more African wildlife. Take the time to catch a few talks and feeds along the way, especially when the queues for the big rides are long.

Pack sun cream in summer and waterproofs year round, and wear comfortable shoes, as you'll be walking a lot. Picnics are a good way to save money, and there are plenty of spots to sit and refuel. Busy times include weekends, bank holidays and the school summer break, so a midweek visit in term time can mean shorter queues.

Getting here without a car is straightforward. Chessington South railway station is a short walk from the park entrance, with trains from London Waterloo. If you're staying for a few days, Hampton Court Palace, Henry VIII's favourite residence, is a short drive away, with its famous maze, gardens and riverside setting. Kingston upon Thames nearby has shops and riverside restaurants, and Bushy Park next to Hampton Court is great for spotting deer.
